title: Tamsin and the Archive
premise: Beatrix Dunmore, the fourth clone of a murdered astrophysicist, has spent eleven years alone tending a deep-space beacon built from her original's stolen research. When gravity stutters across the system for nine seconds, a dying courier named Elias Voss crashes into her orbit carrying a message encoded in her own genome — proof that the war's founding atrocity was staged, and that her original was killed to bury it. As the beacon's failing reactor counts down toward detonation, Beatrix must choose between preserving the last copy of herself and broadcasting the message that could end the war. She sends it, dies in the blast, and wakes as clone five in a hospital on the armistice station — greeted by Elias's sister and the first found family she has ever had.
about_author: Coral Zhou is a former radio telescope technician who writes science fiction about people who maintain things nobody thanks them for. She lives near an observatory and insists the best stories start with a hum you can't explain.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Routine maintenance on the beacon is interrupted when gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, hurling tools, water, and Beatrix herself against the walls. In the aftermath, her sensors catch an unpowered hull tumbling toward her. The beat is disorientation sharpening into dread: her ordered world has cracked open.

chapters.title: The Man in the Cargo Net
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She reels in the wreck and finds Elias Voss, shot twice and half-frozen, clutching a data core he refuses to release even unconscious. Tending his wounds, she recognizes her own face in his delirious muttering — he was looking for 'Dunmore.' Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness toward a stranger who knows too much.

chapters.title: What the Original Left Me
chapters.summary: Elias's POV, feverish and fragmented. He remembers the courier run, the ambush, and the woman who gave him the core: a scientist who said only a Dunmore clone could read it. He wakes distrustful, testing whether this clone is loyal to the Archive or to whoever killed her original. Beat: paranoia wrestling with gratitude.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Pressed by Elias, she audits the beacon's construction logs and finds no commissioning record — it was built off-book with her original's research, a transmitter disguised as a navigation aid. Someone wanted it here, waiting. Beat: the vertigo of learning your whole life was someone else's contingency plan.

chapters.title: A Message Written in Bloodlines
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The core unlocks only against live Dunmore genetic material. Inside: flight recordings proving the war's opening massacre was staged by the victorious Coalition, plus a dead-man's switch keyed to the reactor. Beatrix realizes the beacon isn't just a transmitter — it's the fuse. Beat: horror curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Dark
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A Coalition interdiction ship arrives, pinging politely, then not politely. Elias recognizes their commander from the ambush. The pair must decide: run, hide, or let the ship dock and search. Beat: claustrophobic tension as they fake a derelict station while hiding a living fugitive.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Talking to Myself
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, quiet chapter. While the hunter ship waits, she and Elias trade histories over ration tea. She confesses the loneliness of being a copy maintained like equipment; he admits he volunteered for the run because his sister is on the losing side. Beat: two guarded people discovering they are each other's first real audience.

chapters.title: The Reactor Speaks
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The dead-man's switch activates early — tampered remotely by the hunters' scan — starting a countdown to overload unless the message transmits. Broadcasting requires aiming the dish through the debris ring during a meteor swarm. Beat: the trap snapping shut, converting choice into deadline.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Coalition commander Ilsa Reyes's POV. Reyes boards under truce, offering Beatrix protection and a quiet life in exchange for the core. She genuinely believes destroying the message prevents a worse war. Beat: an antagonist rendered sympathetic — duty versus truth, both wearing uniforms.

chapters.title: The Fourth Copy's Bargain
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix stalls Reyes while Elias preps the dish, offering a partial decryption as bait. Privately she calculates what survival costs: every hour of delay spends reactor margin she can't replace. Beat: cold clarity — she begins planning around her own death.

chapters.title: Everything I Inherited
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, original Beatrix Dunmore's POV via recovered logs. The original discovered the staged massacre, built the beacon, and recorded goodbye messages to her clones — apologizing for making them custodians. Present-day Beatrix listens alone. Beat: grief for a woman she never met who is also, somehow, herself.

chapters.title: Mutiny at Docking Bay Two
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A young Coalition tech, shown a fragment of the evidence, sabotages the hunter ship's weapons rather than fire on the beacon. Reyes arrests her own crew, and the standoff fractures. Beat: hope arriving sideways — the message works on people before it ever broadcasts.

chapters.title: The Debris Ring Run
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, action climax build. With the reactor at critical, Beatrix pilots a maintenance skiff through the meteor swarm to manually align the dish, Elias flying cover in the repaired wreck. Beat: terror transmuted into purpose — every near-miss paid for with pieces of the ship and her nerve.

chapters.title: What Reyes Knew All Along
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Confronted with full evidence, Reyes reveals her orders came from someone who wanted the beacon destroyed before it spoke — her mission was always cover-up, not rescue. She stands down her guns but cannot stop the remote kill-switch. Beat: an enemy becoming a witness.

chapters.title: Countdown at Zero Hour
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Transmission begins; the reactor passes the point of no return. Elias begs her to evacuate in the skiff; the math says there's room for one. She locks him out of the airlock cycle and keeps transmitting. Beat: devastating tenderness — she chooses the message, and him, over herself.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Light
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs across the system. The broadcast hits every receiver simultaneously; ships, stations, and fleets go silent for exactly nine seconds — mirroring the gravity flicker. On the beacon, the reactor breaches. Beat: catharsis and loss fused, the story's central image paying off.

chapters.title: Ash Orbit
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Adrift in the skiff, Elias watches the beacon's debris field glitter and refuses rescue hails until Reyes's ship forces the issue. He carries the transmission's confirmation codes and Beatrix's final log. Beat: hollowed-out grief, the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Armistice Station
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Weeks later, ceasefire talks stall because both sides dispute the evidence. Elias testifies; Reyes corroborates at the cost of her career. The war doesn't end cleanly — it pauses, trembling. Beat: bitter realism, victory that feels like unfinished business.

chapters.title: Growth Medium Number Five
chapters.summary: New clone's POV, waking in an Archive facility. Clone five surfaces with fragmented memory echoes — Beatrix's last hours bleeding through. An Archive handler offers her the old life: another beacon, another silence. Beat: uncanny rebirth shadowed by the question of whether she is her, or hers.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Waited
chapters.summary: Clone five's POV. Elias's sister Maren arrives at the facility with Elias's confirmation codes and a demand: the Archive will not recycle this clone back into service. Found family forms in a corridor — a stranger's brother, a stranger's sister, all that remains of a dead woman's courage. Beat: warmth after long cold.

chapters.title: Tamsin
chapters.summary: Clone five's POV. Offered the name Beatrix again, she chooses instead the name her original used privately in her logs — Tamsin — claiming inheritance without erasure. She and Maren petition to finish the beacon's work openly, as witnesses rather than custodians. Beat: self-authorship, the theme of inheritance resolved into choice.

chapters.title: The Message That Ended the War
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, epilogue. One year later, the rebuilt beacon transmits openly — testimony, names, apologies — and the ceasefire hardens into treaty as the last holdouts stand down. Tamsin tends the dish with Maren and Elias beside her, and for the first time the beacon answers back: acknowledgments from a listening system. Beat: peace earned, family kept, survival finally worth its price.
